findings.title: Delete builds a contextual logger but passes the unscoped `d.Log` into the context
findings.description: In `Delete`, `log` is built with `name`, `kind`, and `method`, but the next line is `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. The enriched `log` is never placed in the context, so downstream logging in the storage call loses those values. Every other method in this diff uses `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

findings.title: Delete passes `name` where the kind value belongs to the storage duration metric
findings.description: After a successful storage delete, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. The third argument is the kind label, but `name` is passed where the other methods pass `options.Kind`. This mislabels the metric series.

findings.title: Update records a storage failure as a legacy duration
findings.description: In the error branch after `d.Storage.Update`, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. The failed call was to storage, so this should be `recordStorageDuration`. The legacy and storage metrics are now swapped for this path.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records the legacy goroutine duration with the storage recorder
findings.description: Inside the goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` records a legacy call with the storage recorder. It should be `recordLegacyDuration`, matching the Create, Delete, and Update goroutines.

findings.title: TestMode3_Create failure case sets up the legacy mock but not the storage mock
findings.description: The case named "error when creating object in the unified store fails" configures `setupLegacyFn` with a `Create` expectation and leaves `setupStorageFn` nil. The code under test calls `d.Storage.Create` first, so the storage mock has no expectation for it. The fixture does not match the path the test claims to exercise.

findings.title: TestMode3_List case name says List is not implemented, but List is now implemented
findings.description: The first case is named "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented", but this diff replaces the stub with a real `d.Storage.List` call. The name contradicts what the case now checks: a storage error propagates.

findings.title: Update test references `updatedObjInfoObj` while the removed commented test used `UpdatedObjInfoObj`
findings.description: The new test calls `updatedObjInfoObj{}` with a lowercase initial. The removed code used `UpdatedObjInfoObj`. I could not check the other test files in this session. If no lowercase type is defined in the package, this will not compile. Please confirm the identifier.
